title: Ink Starvation in Inkjet Printers: Causes and Troubleshooting
seoTitle: Ink Starvation in Inkjet Printers: Troubleshooting | FOREACH
description: Trace ink starvation during long print runs. Use nozzle checks, tank level, filter pressure drop, bubbles and measured pump flow to locate the supply fault.
coverAlt: Ink supply diagnostic diagram tracing the reservoir, pump, filter and printhead to locate low level, bubbles and missing print lines
deck: Ink starvation occurs when ink reaches the printhead more slowly than the head consumes it. If one color fades during a long, high-coverage print and recovers after a pause, save the nozzle check and watch the tank level as the fault develops. Then trace the supply line for a restriction or incoming air, and measure flow under the print load that caused the dropout.
scope: This guide covers industrial piezoelectric drop-on-demand inkjet systems. Use the machine’s circuit diagram to identify its reservoirs, pressure controls and any return line. Use the printhead maker’s priming procedure and pressure limits. Continuous inkjet machines have a different ink circuit and service procedure.

sections.title: Does nozzle dropout indicate ink starvation?
paragraphs: Compare a nozzle check taken before the run with one taken as soon as the color fades. A cluster of missing jets that grows with print coverage and recovers after idle time points toward a supply shortfall. If exactly the same jets are missing on a cold start and after a pause, check the nozzle plate and the head’s drive diagnostics before opening the ink line.
Note whether the fault follows a color, a single head or every head on one manifold. That observation tells you whether to start at a head branch or at the shared supply.

sections.title: What order should an ink supply inspection follow?
paragraphs: Start at the reservoir serving the affected color. On a machine with a sub-tank, watch whether its level falls throughout the failing run and rises again during the pause. If it does, start with the refill branch. If the level stays within its normal band, follow the line from that tank to the affected heads.

paragraphs.label: supply, return and circulation paths
paragraphs.suffix: on the machine’s diagram. Identify the tank vent, pump, filters, valves and any damper or regulator in their actual order. Record valve positions and control settings before isolating or opening a line under the equipment’s service procedure.

checks: Check ink level, intake submergence and reservoir venting, including changes at low operating level.
Check valve positions, flow direction, kinks, pinched tubing and recently replaced filters or seals.
Observe accessible, approved sections of tubing; record where bubbles first appear and complete the specified priming procedure.
Under the failing print load, record available pump inlet, outlet and head-side measurements.
After restoring supply, check the nozzle pattern and adjust controls only within the equipment limits.

sections.title: How can filter and tubing resistance cause starvation during longer runs?
paragraphs: A partly loaded filter can pass enough ink for a nozzle check yet restrict supply during a solid fill. At approved taps on either side of the filter, subtract downstream pressure from upstream pressure. Compare that drop with the clean-filter baseline at the same measured flow and ink temperature. As flow falls, even a loaded filter can show a modest pressure drop.

paragraphs.label: industrial inkjet filtration and check-valve guide
paragraphs.suffix: to distinguish an upstream prefilter from the final filter specified for the head. Include the tube, valve or connector in the investigation if the pressure taps span those parts as well.

paragraphs.prefix: For a refill line with 3.2 mm ID tubing, the
paragraphs.label: F-PE-60-32-PP-N inline filter
paragraphs.suffix: is a candidate for coarse filtration. Its specified 40–60 µm range applies to the filter element. Verify ink and cleaning-fluid compatibility and measure the pressure drop at the refill flow. Keep the head manufacturer’s specified final filtration in place.

sections.note: Keep the specified filtration in production. Component-isolation comparisons require an approved test circuit that protects the printhead from unfiltered ink.

sections.title: How do you locate recurring air bubbles in ink lines?
paragraphs: After a tank change, prime the line as specified and record the first place bubbles reappear. If a clear section upstream of a joint stays full while bubbles keep appearing just downstream, inspect that joint and its seal. A suction-side joint can draw air while its outside stays dry. Check one connection at a time.

paragraphs.prefix: During an approved test with clear fluid and transparent tubing, the
paragraphs.label: ABD optical air bubble detector
paragraphs.suffix: can help log when air first passes a test point. Match the groove to the tubing OD and verify the alarm with the target bubble size. The published optical conditions require transparent media. For opaque white or dark ink, use the machine’s leak test and an ink-compatible measurement method validated for that ink.

paragraphs: Visible bubbles and dissolved gas require different checks. Priming displaces air pockets with ink. Where a degasser is fitted, follow its vacuum-side and membrane checks separately.

figure.alt: Three FOREACH ABD optical detectors with covers open to show their different tubing grooves
figure.caption: The clear test line sits in the detector groove. Select the groove for the tubing outside diameter before checking the optical response with the approved transparent test fluid.

checks: Check whether the intake becomes exposed and whether filling or agitation brings air to it.
Recheck filter seals, closed bleed ports and complete priming after maintenance.
Isolate suspect connections one at a time while keeping other conditions unchanged.
After correcting the source, prime again and compare flow, pressure and print results.

sections.title: What should you measure when the ink pump runs but delivery remains low?
paragraphs: Measure flow at the affected branch and record pump inlet and outlet pressures at the same time. In a recirculating system, separate ink sent back to the tank from ink consumed by printing. Total loop flow alone can conceal a shortfall at one head.

paragraphs.prefix: If the motor runs and flow falls to zero, follow the
paragraphs.label: liquid diaphragm pump no-flow checks
paragraphs.suffix: for priming, inlet supply and valve operation. Use an ink-compatible meter or the machine’s test circuit with representative backpressure. Opening the discharge into a cup removes the filter and head load from the measurement.

sections.title: How should supply, return and nozzle meniscus pressures be checked together?
paragraphs: On a recirculating head, the pressure difference between the inlet and return drives ink through the head. The nozzle meniscus responds to pressure relative to ambient at nozzle height. Record the printhead maker’s specified tap positions, reference and limits. A reading at the pump outlet includes the pressure needed to overcome losses farther downstream.

paragraphs.prefix: For an upstream pressure trace, consider the
paragraphs.label: PDM5 absolute pressure sensor
paragraphs.suffix: if its wetted materials, range, accuracy and sampling suit the test. To compare an absolute reading with a gauge-pressure limit, subtract the ambient pressure measured at the same time and account for any height difference. Use an instrument with sufficient accuracy for the head’s narrow meniscus window.

paragraphs.prefix: If pressure oscillates while average flow holds steady, record a trace through the dropout and compare it with the
paragraphs.label: diaphragm pump pulsation measurement procedure
paragraphs.suffix: . Keep the original sample rate and any display-averaging settings with the record.

sections.note: Make pressure adjustments only within the machine and printhead maker’s limits after checking the ink supply and recurring air ingress.

sections.title: How should DPL30 and DPL60 be evaluated before replacing an ink pump?
paragraphs: Evaluate a different pump only after a sound inlet, a serviceable filter and complete priming still leave measured flow below the requirement. Set the target at the working pressure difference and drive voltage. Record how much the ink level falls during the run and how quickly the refill branch must restore it.

paragraphs.label: DPL30-DB liquid diaphragm pump
paragraphs.suffix: has a specified free flow of 300 mL/min with purified water. Use its flow–pressure curve to screen a candidate for the measured load.

paragraphs.label: DPL60-DB liquid diaphragm pump
paragraphs.suffix: has a specified free flow of 600 mL/min under the same reference medium. Both models list 100 kPa as a separate rated pressure. The data sheets do not specify either free-flow value at 100 kPa.

paragraphs.label: 300 vs 600 mL/min ink pump selection guide
paragraphs.suffix: to compare the two candidates. Check the selected wetted materials against both the ink and cleaning fluid, then measure delivered flow with the actual filter, tubing, operating temperature and restart cycle.

sections.title: How do you verify a repair and document ink starvation for a supplier?
paragraphs: Repeat the job that produced the fault with the same media, print mode, ink temperature and starting tank level. Run it beyond the original time to dropout. Compare nozzle checks before and after the run alongside the tank level, flow and pressure trace. A repair should restore sustained delivery within the machine’s limits and remove the original failure pattern.

paragraphs.label: white ink circulation and restart procedure
paragraphs.suffix: for pigment settling. Send the records below to the pump or machine supplier if the pattern returns.
